title: London's 'almost toxic' housing market might not give investors the returns they are looking for
主要内容: London's housing market, described as 'almost toxic,' may not deliver the returns investors are seeking. Analysts suggest that limited price growth in the UK's capital, combined with Brexit-related uncertainties and higher taxes, has made London less attractive for investment. Tom Sharman of NatWest noted that while central London prices have corrected, outer boroughs with better affordability and connectivity could benefit from policies supporting first-time buyers. Data from LSL Acadata shows significant price drops in areas like Southwark and Westminster, though CBRE reported a 1% increase in Southwark. Despite these challenges, the new build sector remains a potential bright spot. Thomas Schneider of BrickVest blamed Brexit for the decline in London's housing prices, highlighting the city's uncertainty compared to other UK cities like Liverpool. CBRE attributed slower sales in 2017 to the introduction of additional stamp duty, which impacted the latter half of the year.
